Tuesday, February 9, 2021  5:30 PM  Teleconference

NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN that the Mayor and Commission Chairs have called a special joint meeting of the
City Council, Planning Commission and Park & Activities Commission, to be called to order via teleconference at
5:30 p.m. on Tuesday, February 9, 2021. The agenda for the special meeting with the items of business to be
transacted or discussed is set forth below.
Posted by the office of the City Clerk on Thursday, February 4, 2021.

NOTE:  PUBLIC PARTICIPATION INFORMATION
  Pursuant to the Governor's Executive Order N-29-20 and current State and County Public Health Orders,
  City Council Members will be participating via teleconference.
  - City Council meetings are recorded and live-streamed on the City’s website at www.rhe.city and
  available for viewing thereafter, and televised on Cox 33 and Frontier FiOS 38 on Wednesday and Friday
  following the meeting.
  - Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1-669-900-6833) from any phone,
  Meeting ID: 853 8571 7140 Meeting Password: 066081. (Please note you will not have the ability to
  speak using the call-in option from a phone line.)
  - Public correspondence may be emailed to the City Clerk at cityclerk@rollinghillsestatesca.gov. Emails
  received before 5:00 p.m. the night of the Council meeting will be forwarded to the City Council for their
  consideration and included as part of the record.
  - Members of the public may comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes &
  Videos” page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/MeetingAgendas). Once the agenda is published, there
  will be an “eComment” button next to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to
  the City’s SpeakUp page. After you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda.
  These comments can be seen by the public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the
  record.
  - Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting may join the Zoom meeting by accessing the
  Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store),
  by entering the following credentials: Meeting ID: 853 8571 7140, Meeting Password: 066081. Members
  of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the following
  process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at the
  lower portion of your screen. The City Clerk will send you a chat message to identify which item on the
  agenda you would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.
  - Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city.

SPECIAL JOINT CITY COUNCIL, PLANNING COMMISSION
  AND PARK & ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING
  FEBRUARY 9, 2021

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

A Special meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order
by MAYOR ZUCKERMAN at 5:33 p.m. via teleconference, pursuant to the Governor’s
Executive Order N-29-20.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Stegura, Schmitz, Huff, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

City Council Members Absent:  None

Planning Commission Members Present: Medawar, Schachter, Yoo, Carman, Scott, Elder

Planning Commissioners Absent: Zigrang

P&A Commissioners Present: Bain, McCormick, Persichina, Romanelli, Ciarolla, Pope

P&A Commissioners Absent: Retz

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Community Services Supervisor Cynthia Morquecho
  Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit
  Interim City Clerk Carrie Gallagher

4.  PUBLIC COMMENT/PUBLIC PRESENTATION

  NONE

5.  DISCUSSION ITEMS

A.  CONCEPTUAL DESIGN FOR GEORGE F CANYON NATURE CENTER

Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material)

Palos Verdes Peninsula Land Conservancy (PVPLC) Executive Director Adrienne Mohan
was introduced to provide a brief summary of operations at the Nature Center.

PVPLC Executive Director Mohan explained the partnership between the City of Rolling Hills
Estates and the Land Conservancy in regards to the role they play at the Nature Center
including but not limited to hosting field trips for local school children, facilitating scout troop
projects and added that they have lead nature walks for both children and adults. She noted
safety concerns at the Center including a lack of restrooms, plumbing and pest issues as
well as accessibility concerns for individuals with disabilities, and added that the redesign is
desperately needed to continue serving the community. She noted PVPLC’s commitment to
helping City staff to with seeking funding opportunities to help implement the project.

Architect representative Rick Espana showcased changes from the 2019 design plan to the
2021 design. He noted updated goals and objectives including the goal to ensure the facility
fits the character of the existing neighborhoods. He discussed the budget concerns and the
role they played in the updates. Mr. Espana used a Power Point presentation to better help
display design renderings. He noted a flexible design to better serve the community that

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES – SPECIAL JOINT PLANNING AND P&A COMMISSION MEETING
FEBRUARY 9, 2021
 would serve as a Nature Center by day and a community event facility when the Nature
Center is not in use if the City so wished to use it in that manner.

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN invited questions from Council and Commission Members.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF questioned page 10 of the revised site plan specific to the use
of a privacy screen or gate and location of such, Mr. Espana noted they intend to use
landscaping to create privacy noting that it currently is not shown within the renderings.
Further discussion ensued regarding privacy gates and the potential for a landscape design
plan in the future.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA questioned the revised site plan specific to the bus turnout
and drop off, she voiced concern over east bound bus travel and turn around locations, Mr.
Espana noted the challenges they face and stated they explored all options and the current
proposal will be further explored with the City Traffic Engineer.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA encouraged fundraising discussions noting that the grants
and funds currently secured are less than 1/3 of the total costs. She added that members of
the public were wishing to comment of the project as well.

Commissioner Bain stated safety concerns specific to elevation of the Community Room
deck, she wished to get more details on the proposed deck fencing as well as on the area
below the deck. Mr. Espana explained that entry onto the deck is at ground level but changes
by eight feet due to elevation change, he noted plans for a guard rail on the deck as well as
plans for landscape and a security gate below specifically to discourage lingering under the
deck. Commissioner Bain asked for clarification for space below the view deck, Mr. Espana
further noted that they are in the details phase and that is yet to be fully designed.

Commissioner Carmen questioned whether thought had been made to uses of the building,
hours of operation, gate operation, and capacity levels specific to parking concerns for
weekend use of the facilities. Additionally she noted concern for ongoing operational
expense. Assistant City Manager Davis stated that future discussions involving the Land
Conservancy will take place, PVPLC Executive Director Mohan added that current
operations were Friday through Sunday 10:00am to 14:00pm and occasionally mid-week for
field trips.

Assistant City Manager Davis noted that the current available 20 parking spaces
accommodate the current use level however the City is exploring other parking options for
a potential for that use to increase in the future.

Commissioner McCormick asked Mr. Espana for additional drawings of the exhibit area and
asked if the larger area would allow for additional exhibits; Mr Espana noted not yet having
renderings specific to exhibits and noted that the larger space would allow for many more
options that have yet to be explored.

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN noted the importance of having a budget in place and in regards to
parking concerns he requested the design of a more permanent parking solution to
accommodate electric vehicles and handicap spaces suggesting permeable surface be used
in the design.

PVPLC Executive Director Mohan noted having no intention to expand on additional
programing rather to serve the current programming.

Commissioner Scott referred to the Nature Center as a “low energy use facility” and
questioned whether discussion has been had over revenue generating roof photovoltaic cell
use. He pointed out the omission of a maintenance area and voiced concerns over unwanted
loitering near the underside of the deck and class room area.

Commissioner Bain encouraged additional discussion regarding a potential for the facility to
go beyond the current use to become a revenue generating facility.

Assistant City Manager Davis noted that there has been no formal discussion pertaining to
use of the facility for generating revenue. She added this would be a future policy discussion.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES – SPECIAL JOINT PLANNING AND P&A COMMISSION MEETING
FEBRUARY 9, 2021
 COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA shared use demands of the library Community Room,
noting pre COVID-19, all rooms were booked continuously, and she supports additional uses
of the Nature Center grounds for revenue generating options.

Commissioner Medawar inquired on issues specific to security cameras and lighting noted
that overlooking these items could pose a liability to the City if it is overlooked.

Mr. Espana noted a small part of the budget was designated for security however security
will be further discussed during a higher design study in the future.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ noted that programmatic uses will need to be determined
before moving forward on issues raised during tonight’s meeting.

Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba noted that an environmental
analysis will be required as direction is provided and that traffic impacts and parking needs
will be determined at that time.

Public Comment

John R, Rolling Hills Estates voiced gratitude to City staff for working through the public’s
concerns and voiced his own concern over pedestrian street crossings in the area.

Nancy Wildman, Horseman’s Association Member voiced concern for the rendering of the
hitching post location and suggested a small corral be designed in its place or move the
location further from the street.

Mr. Espana concurred and stated that the design element would be further discussed and
added he welcomed public input on the issue.

Jennifer Whynaucht, Hitching Post resident, voiced concern over horse crossing to reach
the arena area and asked for assurance that equestrian safety concerns would be
addressed.

Mr. Espana discussed bollard options to close the area to cars while allowing access to
equestrians.

Mr. Moilanen, Hitching Post resident, voiced parking concerns in the area due to overflow
from outside the area.

Commissioner McCormick inquired on plans for bicycle parking.

Assistant City Manager Davis having received a public comment by phone made note for
the record.

City Manager Grammar thanked everyone for their input, he noted that all comments and
concerns would be considered as the process moves forward.

6.  ADJOURNMENT

At 7:03 P.M. MAYOR ZUCKERMAN adjourned the Special Joint City Council meeting to the
next regular City Council meeting to commence immediately for the purpose of a Regular
meeting.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Carrie Gallagher, CMC  Steve Zuckerman
Interim City Clerk  Mayor

FEBRUARY 9, 2021
